name: Lightbend, Inc. (formerly Typesafe; d/b/a Akka)
subcategory: JVM reactive frameworks (Akka; formerly Scala and Play tooling)
origin_detail: Founded in 2011 as Typesafe by Martin Odersky (creator of Scala), Jonas Bonér (creator of Akka, begun in 2009) and Paul Phillips; HQ San Francisco. Renamed Lightbend in February 2016 and now 'doing business as Akka' (date not given). CEO Tyler Jewell.
openness_notes: Akka was Apache-2.0 from its first releases. On 2022-09-07 Lightbend moved Akka to the Business Source License 1.1: production use needs a commercial licence unless annual revenue is under $25M, and each release reverts to Apache-2.0 after three years. The flagship is source-available: level 1.

license_history.note: First public release Akka 0.5, announced January 2010.
Announced 2022-09-07; free for companies under $25M annual revenue; reverts to Apache-2.0 after 3 years; extra grant for some open-source uses such as Play.

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Pekko graduated to an ASF top-level project on 2024-05-16; Apache Flink, Apache Toree and the Play Framework are adopting it, and 50+ supporting libraries had been released.

risk_events: 2022-2024: Apache Pekko fork, adopted by Flink and Play, graduated at the ASF
robustness: Akka is single-vendor under BSL, but the Apache-licensed lineage continues as Apache Pekko under ASF governance, and each Akka release reverts to Apache-2.0 after three years. Small company: $42M raised in total.
openness_effect_assessment: Lightbend relicensed because Apache 2.0 becomes 'increasingly risky when a small company solely carries the maintenance effort'. The result was a foundation-governed fork that major downstream projects (Flink, Play) moved to, shrinking Akka's open-source footprint. With $42M raised and no disclosed valuation, it is the smallest relicensing case in this group.
key_takeaway: Akka is the small-scale version of the HashiCorp story: a 2022 BSL switch quickly produced an ASF-governed fork (Apache Pekko, top-level by May 2024) that key downstream projects adopted. Even a mid-sized ecosystem now forks into a foundation when its licence closes.
